mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week decline in TRANSIT collapsed from -26.1 points (t-3w to t-2w) to roughly +1 point (t-2w to t-0w), so the mobility contraction has stopped accelerating; with TRANSIT pinned near -85 the shock is exhausted, and RETAIL_REC mean-reverts to a 28-day average above the -79.0 mean of the last window.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT week-on-week change went from -26.1 points (t-3w to t-2w) to +1.1 points (t-2w to t-0w)
regime_hint: tightening restrictions at the contraction trough
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the last-28-day mean of -79.0 while TRANSIT week-on-week change stays within +/-2 points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL staying at or above +30 for three consecutive weeks marks confinement saturation: households have exhausted home-based substitution and begin re-allocating marginal trips to non-essential destinations, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays at or above +30 for a third consecutive week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was +32.4, +32.4 and +33.0 in the last three weekly means, i.e. at or above +30 for three consecutive weeks
regime_hint: hard lockdown with accumulating confinement fatigue
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean does not exceed the last-28-day mean in every instance where RESIDENTIAL stays above +30 for three consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improving while WORKPLACES stays pinned below -80 means recovering trips are local errands rather than commuting; this divergence shows non-work trip demand is already reactivating and predicts higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by at least 2 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES remains at or below -80
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 5.7 points from t-2w (-75.7) to t-0w (-70.0) while WORKPLACES stayed at -80.6
regime_hint: tight lockdown with essential-trip recovery only
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean does not exceed the last-28-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM gains at least 2 points week-on-week with WORKPLACES at or below -80.

mechanism_narrative: Under a regime where outdoor access is relaxed before commercial reopening, PARKS is the first series the policy lever moves; a PARKS upturn therefore leads RETAIL_REC recovery by roughly four weeks because re-opened outdoor corridors pull adjacent retail footfall back.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -77.4 to -76.3 while TRANSIT stayed near its floor at -84.9, so PARKS is the only series already turning
regime_hint: restriction-easing path where outdoor access is unlocked before commercial reopening
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS rises at least 5 points week-on-week, the following 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays at or below the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES never recovering above -79.9 across all four weeks means the weekday commuter and lunchtime population is still absent; with RESIDENTIAL held at +30 or higher, the weekday footfall base of retail corridors keeps shrinking, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remained between -80.7 and -79.9 in all four weekly means
regime_hint: steady-state hard lockdown with no workplace re-entry
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean exceeds the last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES stays at or below -80 and RESIDENTIAL at or above +30.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained GROCERY_PHARM improvement while RETAIL_REC keeps falling identifies the unwind of panic stockpiling: once pantry replenishment is complete, households cut general-merchandise baskets, so RETAIL_REC declines further in the week immediately after the grocery series normalises.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by at least 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 5.7 points from t-2w to t-0w while RETAIL_REC fell a further 2.1 points over the same span
regime_hint: post-panic-buying lockdown where grocery demand has already normalised
failure_condition: In the week after two consecutive GROCERY_PHARM gains of at least 3 points, RETAIL_REC is higher than in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS series turned up (+1.1 points week-on-week) while every commercial series stayed flat, consistent with the spring seasonal transition rather than policy; because park-adjacent high streets seasonally inherit that outdoor traffic, a positive PARKS weekly change leads a higher RETAIL_REC mean over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change turns positive by at least 2 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS week-on-week change turned positive (+1.1 points) between t-2w and t-0w while RETAIL_REC change was negative
regime_hint: spring seasonal transition occurring inside a lockdown
failure_condition: The 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC after a PARKS weekly gain of at least 2 points is not higher than the 28-day mean preceding that gain.

mechanism_narrative: Any easing of movement restrictions first shows up in TRANSIT, which is the fastest-reacting series to a policy change; a TRANSIT rebound of at least 5 points is therefore a necessary precondition, and its arrival together with a WORKPLACES uptick lifts RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points above its t-0w level of -84.9
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -84.9 at t-0w, the least-depressed weekly value in the last three weeks, and WORKPLACES was -80.6
regime_hint: announced restriction easing with a measurable policy step
failure_condition: TRANSIT gains at least 5 points from its t-0w level but the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays at or below the last-28-day mean.
